{{Short description|Canadian roboticist}}
[[Image:Mark Tilden Oslo.jpg|thumb|Mark Tilden in September 2006]]{{Robotic laws}}
'''Mark W.<!--Woodruff?--> Tilden''' is a [[robotics]] [[physicist]] who produces complex robotic movements from simple analog [[logic circuit]]s, often with discrete electronic components, and usually without a microprocessor. He is controversial because of his libertarian [[Laws of robotics#Tilden's laws|Tilden's Laws of Robotics]],<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/1994/09/tilden/|title=Chaotic Robotics|first=Fred|last=Hapgood|magazine=Wired |date=September 1, 1994|via=www.wired.com}}</ref> and is known for his invention of [[BEAM robotics]] and the [[WowWee]] [[Robosapien]] humanoid robot.

==Early career==
Born in the [[United Kingdom|UK]] in 1961, raised in Canada, Tilden started at the [[University of Waterloo]] then moved on to the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] where he developed simple robots such as the SATbot which instinctively aligned itself to the [[magnetic field]] of the Earth, de-mining insectoids, "Nervous Network" theory and applications, interplanetary explorers, and behavioral research into many solar-powered "Living Machines" of his own design.

Tilden later referred to his early robots as "wimpy" for the results of their programming using Isaac Asimov's [[Three Rules of Robotics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.robots-dreams.com/2004/11/three_laws_of_r.html |title=Three Laws of Robotics – Mark Tilden Style &#124; Robots Dreams |accessdate=2014-07-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820040541/http://www.robots-dreams.com/2004/11/three_laws_of_r.html |archivedate=2014-08-20 }}</ref> He accordingly promulgated another set of three rules for what he called "wild" robots, essentially survivalists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.informit.com/imprint/index.aspx?st=61090|title=Que Publishing &#124; InformIT|website=www.informit.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.botmag.com/the-evolution-of-a-roboticist-mark-tilden/|title=The Evolution Of A Roboticist – Mark Tilden|first=Robot|last=Staff|date=December 7, 2010|website=Robot Mag}}</ref>

==Current work==
Having left government service and moved to Hong Kong, Tilden currently works as a freelance robotics designer, consultant and lecturer. His commercial products are marketed through [[Wow Wee|WowWee Toys]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wowwee.com/|title=WowWee® - Astonishing Imagination|website=wowwee.com}}</ref> [[Biomorphic robot]]-based items include B.I.O. Bugs (2001), Constructobots (2002), G.I Joe Hoverstrike (2003), [[RoboSapien]] (2004), [[Robosapien v2]] (2005), [[Roboraptor]] (2005), [[Robopet]] (2005), [[Roboreptile]] (2006), [[RS Media]] (2006, co-developed with Davin Sufer and Maxwell Bogue), [[Roboquad]] (2007), [[Roboboa]] (2007), the humanform [[Femisapien]] (2008), Joebot (2009), and the Roomscooper floor-cleaning robot (2010).

Tilden and his robots have been featured on several television specials, such as "Robots Rising" (Discovery), "The Shape of Life" (PBS), "TechnoSpy" (TLC), "Extreme Machines - Incredible Robots" (TLC), "The Science behind Star Wars" (Discovery), as well as many magazines, newspaper publications, websites, and books.  A comprehensive article on Tilden (December-2010) by Thomas Marsh is viewable online through the "Robot" Magazine website.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://find.botmag.com/121084 |title=The Evolution of a Roboticist - Mark Tilden &#124; Robot Magazine - the latest hobby, science and consumer robotics, artificial intelligence |accessdate=2011-01-30 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110203060006/http://find.botmag.com/121084 |archivedate=2011-02-03 }}</ref>

Tilden also was a technical consultant for the robot scenes in the 2001 movie ''[[Lara Croft: Tomb Raider]]''. His robots are also continuous background props in the TV series ''[[The Big Bang Theory]]''. Movies which feature his robots in prominent roles include ''[[The 40 Year Old Virgin]]'', ''[[Paul Blart Mall Cop]]'' and ''[[X-Men: The Last Stand]]''. Tilden appeared in the 2016 documentary film ''[[Machine of Human Dreams]]'', which showed the work of several prominent technologists based in Hong Kong.
